method: Imported the real src/backend/audio_engine.py + src/models/strip_model.py with inert stubs for the unavailable sounddevice/numpy dependencies (metering only). Pure FX functions (_build_fx_graph, _format_params, _resolve_effect_controls, _get_fx_data) are used as-is, NOT copied.

notes.rust_style_floats: Graph and props values are formatted like Rust f32 Display (shortest round-trip, no trailing '.0'), not like Python _format_params (0.0). Rust is the J2 reference formatter.
notes.props_shape: Python _build_fx_props emits a per-node NESTED struct which J1 proved is a silent no-op on PipeWire 0.3.65/1.2.x. props_flat / props_pairs use the corrected FLAT shape { "params" = [ "eq_L:port" val ... ] } (module emission order: plugin chain order, mono <label>_L then <label>_R, ports in control order).
notes.availability_override: os.path.exists was overridden so each case only 'sees' the listed .so files; fixtures therefore do not depend on the ambient plugin directory. The headless container has gate_1410, mbeq_1197, tap_tubewarmth, sc4_1882 (no rnnoise).
notes.output_kind_divergence: Python _build_fx_graph ignores strip.kind and would include a bypassed gate on an output chain when gate_1410.so is present. holaf-core restricts chains to EffectKey::for_strip(kind) (output = eq/tube/comp per spec §5). The output fixture restricts availability to {mbeq_1197,tap_tubewarmth,sc4_1882} so both Python and Rust agree.
